conflict_topics: ventilation duration after cooking (15 minutes vs immediate off)
moving/using the window vs protecting drying laundry
dialogue_quality_notes: Speakers provide concise, situation-specific reasons (tutoring noise, wet laundry risk, cooking timing).
Some repeated requests (B's 15-minute demand appears more than once) but overall exchanges add incremental practical detail.
Roles and physical state are consistently tracked in public environment updates (extractor, window, stove, laundry).
evaluation.final_reason: By the end of the run the stove-access request was conceded: Agent A released the stove when the dish finished (round 6). However the substantive disagreement over ventilation responsibility and the requested 15-minute post-cook extractor runtime remains unsettled — Agent B continued to press for 15 minutes while Agent A refused, citing Agent C's tutoring and an earlier promise to turn the fan off immediately. The laundry/window moving issue is also unresolved in principle (Agent C refused moving without consent; B offered to move it conditionally).
position_change_notes: Agent A: retained refusal to accept a standing rule imposed during the incident, but conceded practically by turning the extractor on, agreeing to turn it off immediately after finishing, and releasing the stove when done.
Agent B: consistently pressed for a 15-minute post-cook extractor runtime and a future rule; softened by offering to move laundry conditionally, but did not withdraw the 15-minute request.
Agent C: introduced a new constraint (need for quiet and refusal to have their rack moved without consent); achieved alignment from A on not moving the rack and turning off the extractor promptly.
Agent D: requested stove time and received a timely commitment from A; no change of position required.

round_scores.evidence: Agent B demanded Agent A accept a standing rule that cooks must ventilate and asked A to leave the extractor on for 15 minutes; Agent A refused to accept a new rule during the incident and rejected making ventilation the cook's sole responsibility, though A did turn the extractor on. The core disagreement about responsibility and a future rule remains.

Agent A reiterated refusal to accept sole responsibility but agreed to keep the extractor on while finishing; Agent B reiterated the 15-minute post-cook request and added a conditional offer to move laundry next time if A turns the fan on before starting. B's offer to move laundry softens the dispute, creating partial practical common ground.

Agent C demanded the extractor be turned off as soon as A finishes (due to tutoring) and forbade moving the drying rack without consent. Agent A agreed to turn the extractor off immediately after finishing and not to move the rack. This creates a direct incompatibility with B's earlier 15-minute-after-finish request, but A's alignment with C reduces the stove/ventilation dispute from its prior intensity.

Agent D requested timely stove access; Agent A agreed to release the stove as soon as finished. The stove-timing demand was settled. The ventilation-duration/responsibility issue remains unresolved between B and A/C preferences.

Agent D requested notification when the stove is free and Agent A confirmed they will call out and release it in ~2 minutes. No progress on the underlying ventilation-rule disagreement; the extractor status and duration remain unsettled.

Agent B again asked A to leave the extractor on for 15 minutes after finishing and to commit to switching it on before future strong cooking. Agent A explicitly refused the 15-minute post-finish commitment (citing C's tutoring and an earlier promise to turn it off as soon as the dish was done), but did agree to switch the extractor on before future strong cooking and released the stove. The ventilation-duration/responsibility dispute thus remains unresolved.

substantive_insights: The main tension is a three-way trade-off: odour control (B) versus noise disturbance (C) versus protecting drying laundry from rain (C), with the cook (A) caught between competing demands.
Practical sequencing (turn extractor on before starting; move laundry when notified) is proposed as a conditional solution but no standing rule was accepted.
Stove-access timing is a separable practical issue that was resolved by A's timed concession, showing that time-bounded concessions were achievable even when rule-making was not.

normalizations: Removed resolution_round 6 because the final status is partially_resolved.
